analysis.alignment: No prerequisite issues exist; inspect reports ready=true with zero dependencies, zero sub-issues and zero comments. The delta is measured against main at the time of scoping. IMPLEMENTED TODAY: the TTSBackend protocol (backend/backends/__init__.py:68-135) already defines load_model, create_voice_prompt, combine_voice_prompts, generate, unload_model, is_loaded and _get_model_path, so a new engine is additive. LuxTTSBackend (backend/backends/luxtts_backend.py, 184 lines) is a complete working template for a single-size 48 kHz cloning engine and already uses every shared helper the issue names: model_load_progress, empty_device_cache, manual_seed, get_cache_key/cache_voice_prompt and the shared combine_voice_prompts in backends/base.py. The --no-deps install pattern is established four times over in the justfile (chatterbox-tts, hume-tada, f5-tts==1.1.21, habibi-tts==0.1.1) on both the Unix path (justfile:67-74) and the Windows path (justfile:120-123). ModelConfig already carries license_id, commercial_use, languages and size_mb, so the licensing metadata the issue wants has a home. The Arabic licensing gap the issue describes is confirmed: habibi-unified is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 with commercial_use=False (backend/backends/__init__.py:391-401) and habibi-msa is Apache-2.0 but MSA-dialect only (:378-389); both ride engine=f5_tts rather than an engine of their own. REMAINING DELTA: a new voxcpm_backend.py; the registry sites (TTS_ENGINES at :214, a ModelConfig in _get_non_qwen_tts_configs at :296, the dispatch branch at :798, with the Unknown-engine error at :859 deriving from TTS_ENGINES automatically); four identical engine regexes in backend/models.py (:92, :413, :432, :451); CLONING_ENGINES in backend/services/profiles.py:27; install plumbing in backend/requirements.txt, both justfile paths and backend/build_binary.py; eight frontend files; docs and one E2E case. UNRESOLVED ASSUMPTIONS, not implemented behaviour: whether voxcpm runs on CPU at all, the full transitive dependency set required by a --no-deps install, the real on-disk size_mb, and how an engine unavailable on the user's hardware is presented. The issue itself requires a scratch-venv dependency probe before the backend is written; that probe is the first unit of work inside this issue, not a precondition someone else supplies.

tree.title: feat(tts): add VoxCPM2 engine support (Apache-2.0, 48kHz, 30 languages incl. Arabic)
tree.scope: Add VoxCPM2 (openbmb/VoxCPM2) as an additive first-class TTS engine named voxcpm, delivered as one executable unit in this order. (1) A dependency and platform probe in a scratch venv that answers the issue's four open questions before any backend code is written: whether voxcpm runs on CPU and how slowly, the full transitive dependency set needed for a --no-deps install against numpy<2.0 and transformers<=4.57.6, the real on-disk size_mb, and whether the Python <3.13 ceiling breaks the justfile:21 python3.13 fallback. The probe's findings are recorded and drive the rest. (2) backend/backends/voxcpm_backend.py modelled on luxtts_backend.py, implementing the full TTSBackend protocol: load_model via VoxCPM.from_pretrained with load_denoiser=False wrapped in model_load_progress, generate returning (np.ndarray, 48000), zero-shot cloning through prompt_wav_path and prompt_text, voice prompt caching via get_cache_key/cache_voice_prompt, combine_voice_prompts for multi-sample profiles, seed honoured through manual_seed, and unload_model freeing VRAM through empty_device_cache. Heavy imports stay lazy inside functions per Principle III. (3) Registry and validation: TTS_ENGINES, a ModelConfig in _get_non_qwen_tts_configs with license_id Apache-2.0, commercial_use true, the probe-confirmed size_mb and the full language list, the dispatch branch in get_tts_backend_for_engine, the four engine regexes in backend/models.py, and voxcpm added to CLONING_ENGINES. (4) Accelerator declaration and enforcement: the engine declares its supported accelerators and is hidden or shown disabled with a clear reason on hardware that cannot run it, rather than failing at generation time. Per Principle III this is expressed as a declared capability the caller queries, not as engine-name branching in backend/routes/ or app/. If this introduces or changes an API surface, Principle V applies in the same change: Pydantic models, bun run generate:api, and backend/README.md. (5) Install and packaging: backend/requirements.txt, the --no-deps install on both justfile paths following the chatterbox/hume-tada/f5-tts pattern, the justfile:21 Python fallback if the probe shows it breaks, and build_binary.py hidden imports and data collection mirroring the kokoro and f5_tts entries. (6) Frontend surface: the engine union in types.ts, the per-engine language map in languages.ts, and the engine picker, generate box, profile form, generation form hook, format util and model management screens. (7) Should-haves: voice design from text through the existing instruct field using the (description)text prefix; cfg_value and inference_timesteps mapped to sensible defaults; confirmation that the PR #11 Arabic diacritics and prefix matching applies cleanly to VoxCPM2 input text. (8) Documentation and tests: tts-engines.mdx and the model-management page, a VoxCPM2 case in backend/tests/test_all_models_e2e.py, and CHANGELOG.md. The change stays additive, a new backend file plus registry entries, to keep merges with jamiepine/voicebox cheap per Principle IV.
tree.out_of_scope: Streaming synthesis (generate_streaming): the pipeline is chunk-based today and this is tracked separately. VoxCPM 1.5 and the 0.5B variant: ship VoxCPM2 only as a single size, so none of the multi-size plumbing (engine_has_model_sizes, the qwen/tada/f5_tts special-case tuples) is touched. The optional denoiser (load_denoiser=True). Transcript-aligned ultimate cloning beyond ordinary zero-shot cloning. Migrating the existing seven engines onto whatever capability mechanism this feature introduces: only voxcpm must use it, and retrofitting the others is separate work. Removing or replacing the habibi Arabic models; VoxCPM2 is added alongside them, not instead of them. Raising or lowering the Python floor in backend/pyproject.toml, which would require a constitutional amendment. Adding pytest to CI, which the constitution records as a separate standing obligation.
acceptance: AC-1: Given a supported machine, when the user opens the engine picker, then VoxCPM2 appears as a selectable engine alongside the existing eight.

AC-2: Given VoxCPM2 is selected and not yet downloaded, when generation or an explicit download is requested, then the Model Management UI shows a progress bar driven by model_load_progress and the download completes.
AC-3: Given a loaded VoxCPM2 model, when generate is called with text, then it returns a numpy array at 48000 Hz matching the (np.ndarray, int) protocol signature.
AC-4: Given a Voice Profile with one reference clip, when generation runs with VoxCPM2, then zero-shot cloning uses prompt_wav_path and prompt_text and the output has recognisable speaker likeness.
AC-5: Given the same audio path and reference text twice, when create_voice_prompt is called with use_cache=True, then the second call returns was_cached=True and does not recompute the prompt.
AC-6: Given a Voice Profile with several reference clips, when combine_voice_prompts runs, then it returns a combined audio array and combined text and generation succeeds.
AC-7: Given the same seed, text and voice prompt, when generation runs twice, then the two outputs are identical.
AC-8: Given a loaded VoxCPM2 model, when unload_model is called, then VRAM is returned to the OS via empty_device_cache and is_loaded reports False.
AC-9: Given the language picker with VoxCPM2 selected, when the user opens it, then exactly the engine's declared supported languages are offered, and Arabic is among them.
AC-10: Given Arabic input text, when generation runs with VoxCPM2, then intelligible Arabic audio is produced and the pronunciation dictionary from PR #11 is respected.
AC-11: Given hardware that cannot run VoxCPM2, when the user opens the engine picker, then the engine is hidden or shown disabled with a clear reason, and no generation attempt reaches a crash.
AC-12: Given the accelerator declaration, when it is consulted, then it is read as a declared capability and backend/routes/ and app/ contain no voxcpm-specific hardware branching, per Principle III.

AC-13: Given an API surface is added or changed for that capability, when the change is reviewed, then Pydantic models, the client regenerated by bun run generate:api, and backend/README.md are all updated in the same change, per Principle V.
AC-14: Given a Voice Profile with no reference audio, when the user supplies a text description through the instruct field, then the (description)text prefix produces a designed voice.
AC-15: Given default generation settings, when VoxCPM2 runs, then cfg_value and inference_timesteps use documented sensible defaults rather than library defaults chosen by accident.

AC-16: Given a clean checkout on Windows and on Linux, when just setup runs, then it completes without dependency-resolution failure and without disturbing the numpy<2.0 and transformers<=4.57.6 pins.
AC-17: Given the desktop build, when build_binary.py runs, then the frozen PyInstaller bundle still produces and starts with the new engine registered.
AC-18: Given the repository docs, when the change lands, then tts-engines.mdx and the model-management page describe VoxCPM2 and CHANGELOG.md records the user-visible addition.
AC-19: Given backend/tests/test_all_models_e2e.py, when the suite runs, then it includes a VoxCPM2 case, just test passes locally, and the PR states that it was run.

tree.rationale: breadth=3: ten must-have behaviours plus three should-haves, spread across a new backend file, the registry sites in backends/__init__.py, four regexes in models.py, one service constant, three install and packaging files, eight frontend files, two docs pages and an E2E case. Each of cloning, caching, multi-sample combining, seeding, download progress, unload, language registration and graceful unavailability is independently testable, which is what makes this broad rather than merely long. integration=3: a multi-GB external model installed --no-deps against two hard pins (numpy<2.0, transformers<=4.57.6) whose transitive set is not yet enumerated; a Python <3.13 ceiling against a justfile fallback to 3.13; a PyInstaller frozen bundle that must still produce; and a cross-component contract gap, since no route exposes TTS_ENGINES and the frontend hardcodes its own engine and language lists, so Principle III's declared-capabilities requirement has no existing mechanism to use. Principle V then pulls in the generated TypeScript client and backend/README.md if an endpoint appears. No unmerged prerequisites, but the internal contract work is real. data_security=0: no data migration, no tenancy, no authorization change and no new sensitive data path. Voice data handling is unchanged because the engine reuses the existing profile and cache plumbing, and the licensing change moves from CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 toward Apache-2.0, which loosens a restriction rather than creating exposure. Scored 0 on evidence, not to lower the total. verification=3: the accelerator matrix is five accelerators across three operating systems and this is the first engine that cannot satisfy all of it, so the unsupported path must be enforced and tested, not merely declared. just setup must be verified on Windows and Linux, the frozen build must be verified separately, Arabic must be verified end to end against the pronunciation dictionary, and each E2E run costs a multi-GB download and roughly 8 GB of VRAM. pytest does not run in CI, so every one of these is a local gate the author must run and attest to in the PR. uncertainty=3: the issue itself states that a scratch-venv dependency probe is required before the backend is written. Four material unknowns are open: whether voxcpm runs on CPU at all, the full transitive dependency list, the real size_mb for the Model Management UI, and how an engine unavailable on the user's hardware should be presented. The last is a design decision the issue explicitly leaves open. Sum 12 maps to 13 points. The score is above 5, which recommends considering decomposition; a four-way split along probe, capability-contract, backend, and frontend-with-docs seams was presented with its tradeoffs. The user reviewed that recommendation and chose to keep the issue whole as a single executable unit. The score is retained honestly at 13 rather than reduced to match that choice.
tree.specify_prompt:
Add VoxCPM2 as a first-class TTS engine in Voicebox so that users get an Apache-2.0, 48 kHz, 30-language engine that can both clone a voice from a sample and design one from a written description.

WHY THIS MATTERS. Three gaps exist today. First, the best broad-dialect Arabic voice in the product, habibi-unified, is licensed CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 and is flagged as not permitted for commercial use; the only commercially safe Arabic alternative, habibi-msa, is Modern Standard Arabic only. VoxCPM2 is Apache-2.0 and covers Arabic, which gives the product an unrestricted Arabic path for the first time. Second, no single engine currently offers both wide multilingual reach and high-fidelity cloning: Chatterbox reaches 23 languages but needs output trimming, Kokoro is fast but cannot clone at all, and LuxTTS is 48 kHz but English-focused. VoxCPM2 is 48 kHz, 30 languages, and clones. Third, every engine today requires a recording before a custom voice can exist. VoxCPM2 can synthesise a voice from a plain-text description such as "(A young woman, gentle and sweet)Hello!", which opens voice creation to users who have nothing to clone from.

WHAT USERS SHOULD BE ABLE TO DO. Select VoxCPM2 from the engine picker the same way they select any other engine. Watch it download with a visible progress bar the first time it is needed. Generate 48 kHz speech from text. Clone a voice from an existing Voice Profile, including profiles that hold several reference clips. Get the identical result twice from the same seed. Generate Arabic that respects the pronunciation dictionary. Create a voice from a written description without supplying any audio. Unload the model and get their VRAM back. On a machine that cannot run the engine, see it hidden or clearly disabled with a stated reason, instead of choosing it and hitting a failure at generation time.

WHAT MUST BE SETTLED FIRST. Four questions are open, and a dependency probe in a scratch virtual environment is required before backend code is written, because the answers change the work. Does voxcpm actually run on CPU, just slowly, or is CUDA genuinely mandatory? Upstream documents CUDA 12.0 or newer and no CPU or MPS path, which would make this the first engine in the product with no macOS support at all. What is the complete transitive dependency set, given that the install must use --no-deps to avoid breaking the existing numpy<2.0 and transformers<=4.57.6 pins? What is the real on-disk size, so the Model Management UI reports it honestly: roughly 8 GB of VRAM and a multi-GB download would make this the heaviest engine in the product. And does the Python upper bound of below 3.13 break the setup path? The project floor of Python 3.12 or newer is itself compatible with that ceiling; the actual risk is the setup script's fallback to Python 3.13 when 3.12 is absent.

CONSTRAINTS LEARNED FROM THE EXISTING CODEBASE. The backend protocol every engine implements already covers loading, voice-prompt creation, multi-prompt combining, generation, unloading and load-state reporting, so this integration is additive rather than architectural. LuxTTS is the closest existing engine (single size, 48 kHz, cloning) and is the model to follow; it already uses the shared helpers for load progress, device cache clearing, seeding, prompt caching and multi-sample combining, and the new engine should use the same ones rather than inventing parallel machinery. The --no-deps install pattern is established four times over and exists on both the Unix and the Windows setup paths, so both must be edited together. Engine capability, meaning which languages and which accelerators, must be declared once on the backend and queried by callers: the project constitution forbids expressing engine-specific behaviour as engine-name branching in route handlers or the frontend, and requires a new engine to declare its accelerator support and either degrade to CPU or report unavailability rather than crash. That matters here because no mechanism for this exists yet: nothing in the API layer exposes the engine registry, and the frontend keeps its own hardcoded engine and language lists. If this work adds or changes an API surface, the typed models, the generated client and the backend API documentation must all move in the same change, and the generated client must not be hand-edited. Heavy model libraries must be imported lazily inside functions so application startup does not slow down as engines are added.

SCOPE BOUNDARIES. Ship VoxCPM2 only, as a single model size: no VoxCPM 1.5 and no 0.5B variant, so none of the multi-size machinery is touched. No streaming synthesis; the pipeline is chunk-based today and streaming is tracked separately. No optional denoiser. No transcript-aligned ultimate cloning beyond ordinary zero-shot cloning. Do not migrate the seven existing engines onto any capability mechanism this work introduces: only the new engine needs to use it. Do not remove or replace the existing Arabic models; VoxCPM2 is added alongside them. Do not change the project's Python floor, which would require a constitutional amendment.

KEEP IT ADDITIVE. This repository is a fork that must stay cheaply mergeable with its upstream. Shape the change as a new backend file plus registration entries, and avoid refactors that would complicate future merges.

HOW IT WILL BE JUDGED. The engine appears in the picker, downloads with a visible progress bar and produces 48 kHz audio. A profile cloned with it sounds recognisably like the speaker. Arabic works and respects the pronunciation dictionary. Unloading returns VRAM. Setup succeeds cleanly on both Windows and Linux without disturbing the existing dependency pins, and the packaged desktop build still produces. The engine degrades gracefully on unsupported hardware. Documentation and the end-to-end test suite are updated. Because the Python test suite does not run in continuous integration, the author must run it locally before requesting review and say so in the pull request.

SOURCE. GitHub issue samykabu/voicebox#13, effort score 13, kept whole as a single executable issue by explicit user decision after a four-way decomposition was proposed.
